lines.text: Today you will make games that surprise you, because even you will not know what the computer picks.
Python has extra toolboxes called modules. import random at the top of your program opens the random toolbox.
Now you can use its commands.
random.randint(1, 6) gives a whole number from 1 to 6, like rolling a dice.
Both end numbers can come up.
Every run can give a different number.
random.choice(["rock", "paper", "scissors"]) picks one item from the list at random.
Use it for lucky snacks, random names or computer moves.
Most games repeat the same steps: ask, check, give a hint.
A while loop keeps the game going until the player wins or runs out of tries.
First we import the random toolbox, then randint picks a number from one to six.
Your number may be different every time you run it. That is the fun part!
The choice command picks one snack from the list.
Run it again and the computer might choose jalebi or idli instead.
The player guessed thirty, which is bigger than the secret number.
So the program gives a hint: Too high. Now the player knows to go lower.
The loop keeps asking while the guess is wrong and there are tries left.
Every guess adds one to attempts, so we can tell the player how many tries they took.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
